Most of the time, that conversation produces more heat than light. But the Ibanez TS808HW Hand Wired Tube Screamer enters that debate with a rare credential: it was A/B tested by independent reviewers against the original 1980 TS808 and the standard reissue, and the results were genuinely surprising. GG-ARTICLE-AFTER-INTRO The answer wasn’t that the HW sounded identical to the vintage original. It didn’t, quite. But it sounded different from the standard reissue in ways that were immediately audible — more low-end transparency, fuller overdrive, smoother breakup. The reason, according to engineers who pulled it apart, likely has to do with the absence of a circuit board and its associated trace capacitance. That’s the physics behind the marketing claim. And it’s why the TS808HW occupies a unique position in the Tube Screamer family: it’s Ibanez’s own answer to the boutique modification industry that grew up around the TS circuit, and it’s the only hand-wired Tube Screamer that came straight from the factory in Nagoya. This isn’t a review — it’s a deep look at what the TS808HW is, how it came to exist, who actually plays one, and what it sounds like versus everything else in the Tube Screamer universe. Jump to the Rig ↓ How to Get the Tone ↓ From Circuit Board to Turret Board: The TS808HW’s Origins The Tube Screamer circuit debuted in 1979 when Maxon — the Japanese effects company that designed and manufactured Ibanez pedals — produced the TS808 for the North American market. The original TS808 used a JRC4558D op-amp, a soft-clipping diode configuration, and hand-wired construction on turret boards. Those were the production standards of the era, not a premium feature. Over the following decades, the Tube Screamer evolved through the TS9 , the TS10 , and various budget iterations. The TS9 reissue (1993) and TS808 reissue (2004) both moved to printed circuit board construction — standard modern practice that reduces manufacturing cost and improves consistency. Maxon, the original designer, eventually spun off its own OD808 for those who wanted the Maxon name on the box rather than Ibanez.
